summary: The input read limit changes from 1,048,575 to the contract-required inclusive 1,048,576 bytes. The parser retains the same 1 MiB limit and all existing validation. No correctness or scope defect found by source inspection.

assessment.behavior: submitted/main.my:10 restores the exact allowed boundary using the existing bounded byte reader. No prefix truncation, new input path, floating interpretation of size, or change to JSON/schema/planning behavior is introduced. Existing read and parse errors still return whole-request invalid-request.
assessment.tests: submitted/test_cli.py:73 adds actual stdin calls at limit-1, limit and limit+1 for ASCII and UTF-8 multibyte inputs, checking exact response objects and zero exit through call(). An oversized valid prefix with a non-whitespace suffix is rejected. Malformed closing syntax and a truncated multibyte sequence at the boundary are tested. Existing strict Unicode, nesting, integer, duplicate-key and planner tests remain unchanged. verify.json already executes this test module.
assessment.ownership_and_maintainability: Only an integer argument and explanatory comment change in application code. Buffer consumption and document borrowing remain unchanged. The patch uses the existing standard reader and parser with matching limits.
assessment.scope: Two modified files: the application entry point and its existing CLI tests. No special fixture recognition or unrelated application changes found.
assessment.test_limitations: The truncated UTF-8 fixture also contains an unterminated JSON string, so it does not independently isolate UTF-8 rejection. Existing UTF-8 tests separately exercise malformed sequences; this is not a blocking gap.

limitations: Static source review only; no build or tests executed, no Guardian gate exercised, and standard-library reader implementation was not independently inspected.

Reviewed supplied public brief, contract and library material plus baseline/submitted source and tests. Avoided README, parent trial state, private grading, cases, transcripts and new-run timing information.
